mechanism_narrative: A sustained four-week increase in WORKPLACES mobility, indicating a steady return to office-based work, will directly translate into higher weekday footfall for retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES mobility continues to rise for the next four weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant week-on-week increase in TRANSIT usage signals a broader public comfort with out-of-home activities, driving increased visits to retail and recreation spots over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT increases by more than 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility increases by more than 3 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not show an improvement over the subsequent two weeks, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The combined trend of people spending less time at home (decreasing RESIDENTIAL mobility) and increasing essential outings (rising GROCERY_PHARM mobility) will lead to more combined-purpose trips, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases and GROCERY_PHARM mobility increases for the next four weeks, yet RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of easing lockdown restrictions, the simultaneous and sustained increases in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility indicate a coordinated return to urban centers and public life, which will directly boost RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility continue to rise over the next four weeks within an easing restrictions regime, but RETAIL_REC does not increase, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent four-week decrease in time spent at residential locations directly implies people are spending more time outside their homes, which will naturally lead to increased engagement with retail and recreation venues over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL mobility continues its downward trend for the next four weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A strong week-on-week recovery in GROCERY_PHARM visits indicates increased public comfort with out-of-home activities, which will quickly spill over into non-essential retail and recreation within the next week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM mobility increases significantly, but RETAIL_REC does not show any improvement in the subsequent week, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility remains consistently low while RETAIL_REC shows a slight upward trend, it suggests a behavioral shift where leisure activity is redirected from outdoor public spaces to indoor commercial venues, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below 0% change while RETAIL_REC shows any positive week-on-week change
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility remains low and RETAIL_REC improves, but the overall RETAIL_REC trend over the next two weeks is negative, this hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of increasing public confidence, the combined effect of rising TRANSIT usage and decreasing RESIDENTIAL time signifies a broad return to urban mobility and social interaction, which will positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT mobility rises and RESIDENTIAL mobility falls over the next four weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, this hypothesis is falsified.
